subject: people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
tagline: Neuralink for people who didn't marry their high school sweetheart
one_liner: A brain implant for checking on your high school sweetheart. You've made a surgical commitment to keeping it casual.
brand_voice_notes: Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill read at pipelines/codex-v1/skills/anti-ai-slop/SKILL.md. Speak as a composed hardware company serving adults who insist they are only curious. Describe deliberate cursor control, typing and device pairing in ordinary language. The implant responds to practiced commands; embarrassing consequences follow the user's choices. Keep functional labels plain. All capabilities, packages, prices and users belong to this fictional product from the worst AI studio ever.
demo_screen_concept: One implant companion screen labeled Living room package preview. A narrow device panel shows a simple implant diagram, connection status and three selectable tasks: Cursor training, Draft message and Display pairing. Cursor training presents four fictional yearbook portraits; selecting the highlighted target advances a simulated cursor exercise and updates its accuracy report. Draft message opens a large onscreen keyboard with 'Hey' in the composer, an edit counter and Practice and Reset controls. Practice demonstrates intentional typing without sending anything. Display pairing switches the same fictional wedding photograph between Laptop and Living-room TV; choosing the TV enlarges the newly married spouse until their portrait occupies the display preview. The session report updates with the selected task, practice attempts and output device. Label the interaction as a simulation operated by mouse, touch or keyboard. Keep the implant connection, calibration task, cursor feedback and computer output visible throughout.

hero.h1: You had brain surgery to type 'Hey.'
hero.sub: Maybe connects a brain implant to your computer so you can move the cursor and type by thought. Train on your high school sweetheart's yearbook photo, rehearse a casual greeting, then inspect the person they married on your living-room television.

features.title: Train on a familiar face.
features.blurb: Set their yearbook portrait as the target for your cursor exercises. Each successful selection goes into a weekly progress report. At 43, you're receiving marks for looking at someone you couldn't speak to at 17.

features.title: Make it sound casual.
features.blurb: Use the thought-controlled keyboard to compose a greeting, then rehearse it without sending. Your session report records 184 edits to 'Hey.' You describe the message as spontaneous.

features.title: Use a bigger screen.
features.blurb: Pair the implant with your television and use the cursor to enlarge their wedding photo. You wanted a better look at the person they married. You've given a stranger a sixty-five-inch portrait in your living room.

observations.behavior: Adults revisit an old crush while treating the attention as harmless curiosity.
observations.mechanic: Personalize an implanted computer interface by practicing cursor selection on a familiar yearbook portrait, with accuracy reports after each session.
observations.consequence: A grown adult turns decades of looking at an old crush into formally assessed homework and sends the results home to a parent.

observations.behavior: People want an unexpected message to look effortless, so they rehearse a tiny greeting far beyond its importance.
observations.mechanic: A thought-controlled keyboard offers saved drafts, practice sessions and a visible edit history.
observations.consequence: An implant and four evenings of preparation produce three letters, followed by the discovery that the recipient needs the sender's surname.

observations.behavior: People compare themselves with the person their former sweetheart eventually married and inspect photographs for evidence.
observations.mechanic: Pair the implant with a larger display, then use cursor selection and zoom to examine a wedding photograph.
observations.consequence: Private comparison becomes a household presentation: the unfamiliar spouse occupies the television and the user's family discovers how much Dad knows about him.

source_product_patterns: An implanted brain-computer interface connects neural commands to an external computer.
Initial calibration uses repeated, intentional cursor tasks with visible performance feedback.
A companion interface separates device connection, training and computer-control sessions.
Cursor selection and an onscreen keyboard turn practiced commands into visible computer actions.
Wireless device pairing routes the user's deliberate actions to a selected display.
Session reports show practice attempts, accuracy and the active output device.
editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: Try a practice session. Recognizable product visual: an implant companion interface showing a connected implant diagram, calibration targets, a cursor trace and a computer output panel. Open with the Maybe identity and a small the worst AI studio ever credit, then the headline, explanation and CTA immediately above a broad working preview. Show the yearbook target beside the adult user's session report so the medical investment and adolescent task are understood together. Follow with three open feature passages, customer accounts and a joined package comparison. Proposed artwork one shows a middle-aged adult at a kitchen table carefully studying a yearbook beside a freshly printed cursor-training report; it explains the return to schoolwork. Proposed artwork two shows a wedding guest's face enlarged across a domestic television while family photographs sit beneath it; it explains how private comparison occupies the household. The demo's fictional yearbook portraits and wedding photograph provide selectable content. Keep reports, labels, prices, message text and counters in live text. On mobile, stack device status, active exercise and session results in that order, with the selected task and primary control together.

references.cues: Midnight-blue cloth covers, restrained silver lettering, formal portrait grids, white caption strips and school-color dividers.
references.application: Use midnight blue #172B46, paper white #F5F6F2, silver gray #B8C0CB and oxblood #872E40. Pair Bitter display headings with Public Sans body text and controls. Use consistent portrait crops with generous caption space. Create an original Maybe wordmark without school crests or borrowed branding.

references.reference: A twenty-fifth high-school reunion registration table in a school gym
references.cues: Adult name badges carrying teenage photographs, neatly arranged attendance lists, practical folding-table order and incongruous comparisons between past and present.
references.application: Pair small yearbook portraits with plain adult names and current ages in session records. Use thin rules, flat rectangular panels and orderly lists. Supporting photographs should contain believable contemporary homes and middle-aged adults, with the old portrait acting as the recurring object.

audience_design.landing_application: Give the landing page the measured hierarchy of a reunion commemorative publication: a broad navy opening, large white Bitter headline, concise Public Sans explanation and an oxblood primary action with white text. Place the white companion-interface preview directly beneath the proposition. Alternate open white feature passages with two substantial documentary photographs; attach readable captions outside the images. Use silver rules to join pricing columns. Concentrate nostalgia in portraits, typography and printed reports.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's hardware-to-software sequence: connection status, calibration, intentional control and visible output. Use compact Public Sans labels, white task surfaces, navy navigation and oxblood selection indicators. The training targets resemble a yearbook portrait row, but accuracy, connection and device labels remain ordinary interface text. Keep the implant diagram and live cursor feedback visible so the screen reads as a brain-interface companion rather than a social network. On narrow screens, replace the task sidebar with a labeled selector and stack the same workflow.

design_direction.style: Reunion commemorative editorial: midnight-blue yearbook cover, Bitter slab-serif headings, silver rules, oxblood cursor selections and rectangular portrait sheets.

design_direction.design_review: Compared the supplied seven-entry digest. No matching tuple, crest, logo motif or composition. Retained accessible controls from library hardware guidance; rejected its black/pink space corridor and manifesto because the approved audience requires reunion publication typography and recognizable computer-control tasks. Display fonts remain approved Bitter; Public Sans is supported by Magazine Style library. No new concept or approved copy changes.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: An open yearbook spread whose center fold turns into a deliberate cursor stroke: looking back becomes computer control. A small oxblood endpoint is the selected memory. Silver wordmark on midnight cloth avoids recent tags, cupboards, lifting straps and animal silhouettes.

items.prompt: Create a finished original logo asset for the fictional product "Maybe", a brain-computer companion for adults revisiting their high school sweetheart. Audience visual world: 1998–2003 yearbook covers and twenty-fifth reunion registration tables. Exact spelling: Maybe. No other text, no mockup, no board, no watermark. Two-dimensional professionally designed symbol left and bespoke Bitter-like slab-serif wordmark right, horizontal centered lockup with generous blank margins. Controlled palette paper silver #F5F6F2 and silver #B8C0CB, one small oxblood #872E40 detail, perfectly solid midnight-blue #172B46 background. No crest, heart, brain clipart, letter in a square, Neuralink trademark, sparkle or gradient. Strong enough to work in a 180px wide header and a cropped 32px symbol. Direction A: two facing yearbook pages, their open central fold becomes the bent arrow of a computer cursor; one oxblood selected endpoint. Elegant recognizable open spread silhouette, minimal broad strokes. Give custom letterforms a slightly nostalgic bookish character.
items.verdict: Selected A: exact Maybe spelling, open-book silhouette and cursor are recognizable; legible bookish kerning. Flat background removed faithfully and composition cropped with clear space.

items.transformation: Same alpha silhouette, uniform paper-white recolor.

items.prompt: Use attached image as APPROVED IDENTITY REFERENCE. Preserve its Maybe wordmark letterforms and open-yearbook/cursor symbol if reproduced. Design a polished editorial documentary collage, not a plain photo with a caption. The visual world is a silver-lettered 2001 high school yearbook meeting a contemporary middle-aged household. Midnight #172B46, paper #F5F6F2, silver #B8C0CB, oxblood #872E40. Natural believable photographic people and interiors integrated with deliberate print typography, portrait crops, report-paper layers and spare oxblood selection geometry. Strong hierarchy, generous margins, restrained photographic grain. No generic tech glow, no watermark, no extra copy, no gibberish, no rendered UI screen. Intentional graphic design and layout, full composition preserved. Create an original landscape campaign spread. Large documentary scene of an ordinary 43-year-old woman in a modern kitchen, concentrating on an old yearbook and a freshly printed cursor training report. At left an oversized cropped yearbook portrait of a fictional 17-year-old boy from 2001, clearly printed on aged paper. Compose the portrait, adult, report and typography as a single designed spread, not rectangular photo tiles. Paper report visually bridges teenage portrait and adult effort. Top-left large exactly "Back to school." and smaller exactly "Cursor training". On a graphic report-paper layer use only exactly "4 / 4" and "Targets selected". Small approved Maybe logo bottom right. These are all the allowed words. Formal yearbook typography, one meaningful oxblood cursor selection frame, silver column rules. Contemporary domestic daylight, humor through disproportionate concentration. Landscape 3:2.
items.verdict: Accepted: correctly spelled Back to school, Cursor training, 4 / 4 and Targets selected. Extra 2001 date fits approved yearbook era. Designed paper/report layering and believable adult context, not a plain captioned photograph.

items.prompt: Create one photographic contact sheet with four DISTINCT fictional 17-year-old high school students in 2001. No real people. Two boys and two girls, diverse faces. The order is upper left: Sam, boy with short dark brown hair in navy polo, warm smile; upper right: Nora, girl with curly dark hair and white blouse; lower left: Jamie, boy with sandy hair and school sweater; lower right: Leila, girl with straight dark hair and blue blouse. Perfectly regular 2 by 2 grid, zero gutters, zero borders, each quadrant one head and shoulders studio yearbook photograph on identical neutral blue-gray mottled backdrop. Authentic early 2000s natural flash photography, slight printed grain, not caricature. Faces centered horizontally in each quadrant, head fully inside quadrant. NO TEXT, no labels, logos or watermarks, no graphics, no UI. Square overall composition, four square portraits for deterministic cropping. Natural ordinary teenagers, fully clothed.
items.placement: Source for four demo/landing portrait crops
items.verdict: Accepted: four distinct fictional yearbook faces in ordered quadrants; thin white separators removed from derivatives.
